extracted.intended_audience: users of the Singular computer algebra system (mathematicians / computer-algebra practitioners) working with non-commutative algebra libraries
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in Singular's non-commutative libraries (ncalg.lib, ncdecomp.lib, ncfactor.lib): usage, return values, assumptions, purpose, notes and examples for creating/working with noncommutative rings, modules, GKZ systems, central-character decompositions and factorization routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeUe6
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeUe6([p]); p an optional integer (field characteristic). Return: a ring, describing U(e6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: set up the universal enveloping algebra U(e6) derived from the Chevalley representation; positive/negative roots denoted x(i)/y(i), Cartan elements h(i). Note: activate the returned ring with setring. Example shows invocation LIB "ncalg.lib"; def ncAlgebra = makeUe6(); setring ncAlgebra; and reports number of variables and noncommutative relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeUe7
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeUe7([p]); p an optional integer (field characteristic). Return: a ring, describing U(e7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: produce U(e7) from Chevalley representation with x(i), y(i), h(i). Note: activate with setring. Example demonstrates returned ring, number of vars and many noncommutative relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeUe8
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeUe8([p]); p an optional integer (field characteristic). Return: a ring, describing U(e8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: produce U(e8) presentation from Chevalley representation; use setring to activate; example shows large number of variables (248) and many noncommutative relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeQso3
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeQso3([n]), n an optional int. Purpose: set up U_q(so3) in Klimyk's presentation; if n specified, Q specialized at (2n)-th root of unity. Return: ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: activate this ring with setring. Example: def K = makeQso3(3); setring K; output shows coefficients QQ[Q]/(Q2-Q+1) and noncommutative relations (e.g. yx=(Q-1)*xy+(-Q)*z, etc.). See also related procedures (makeQsl2, makeQsl3).

rubrics_metrics.name: makeQsl2
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeQsl2([n]), n an optional int. Return: ring presenting V_q(sl2) together with ideal Qideal; provides means to create U_q(sl2) as a factor ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: define U_q(sl2) as factor-ring of V_q(sl2) modulo Qideal. Note: output consists of ring and exported ideal Qideal; to create U_q(sl2) execute qring Usl2q = Qideal;. If n specified, q specialized at n-th root of unity. Example and sample relations (KeE, KfE, commutation rules) are shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: makeQsl3
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: makeQsl3([n]), n an optional int. Return: ring presenting V_q(sl3) together with ideal Qideal to form U_q(sl3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: define U_q(sl3) as factor ring of V_q(sl3) modulo Qideal. Note: activate with setring; if n given, quantum parameter q specialized at n-th root of unity. Example includes variables, weights, many noncommutative relations and quotient relations (e.g. k2*l2-1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qso3Casimir
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Qso3Casimir(n [,m]), n an integer, m an optional integer. Return: list (of polynomials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute Casimir (central) elements of U_q(so3) for quantum parameter specialized at n-th root of unity; if m!=0 polynomials normalized. Assume base ring must be U_q(so3). Example shows how to compute and normalized outputs; shows expected polynomial forms for x,y,z.

rubrics_metrics.name: GKZsystem
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: GKZsystem(A, sord, alg [,v]); A intmat, sord, alg string, v intvec. Return: ring (Weyl algebra) with GKZ system and exported ideal GKZid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: define a Weyl algebra and create a Gelfand-Kapranov-Zelevinsky (GKZ) system from integer matrix A, term ordering sord and algorithm alg (uses toric lib algorithms 'ect','pt','blr','hs','du'); optional weight vector v. Note: activate output ring with setring; GKZid contains actual equations. Example reproduces example from SST book; prints GKZid and Weyl relations (d(i)x(i)=x(i)d(i)+1). See toric lib for input constraints and allowed orderings.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncdecomp.lib (library overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Library: ncdecomp.lib. Purpose: Decomposition of a module into its central characters; algorithms for central character decomposition into generalized weight modules w.r.t. the center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and background: based on ideas of Khomenko and Levandovskyy. Overview lists procedures CentralQuot, CentralSaturation, CenCharDec, IntersectWithSub and describes intended application and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: CentralQuot
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: CentralQuot(M, G), M a module, G an ideal. Assume: G is an ideal in the center of the base ring. Return: module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute the central quotient M:G := { v in A^n | z*v in M for all z in G }. Note: output module not necessarily given in a Groebner basis. Example demonstrates use with U(sl2) and computing R = CentralQuot(I,G). See also CentralSaturation and CenCharDec.

rubrics_metrics.name: CentralSaturation
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: CentralSaturation(M, T), M a module, T an ideal in the center. Return: module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute the central saturation M:T^infty by repetitive application of CentralQuot. Note: output not necessarily a Groebner basis. Example shows typical workflow and use of std() and vdim() on output. See also CentralQuot and CenCharDec.

rubrics_metrics.name: CenCharDec
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: CenCharDec(I, C); I a module, C an ideal (generators of center). Return: a list L where each entry (if finite decomposition exists) contains three records: L[*][1] (ideal) central character as maximal ideal, L[*][2] (module) Groebner basis of weight module, L[*][3] (int) vector space dimension (-1 if infinite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute finite decomposition of I into central characters or determine that no finite decomposition exists. Note: actual decomposition is sum of L[i][2]; warning messages if no finite decomposition. Example demonstrates decomposition for U(sl2) and a counterexample (no finite decomposition). See also CentralQuot and CentralSaturation.

rubrics_metrics.name: IntersectWithSub
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: IntersectWithSub(M, Z), M an ideal, Z an ideal (consisting of pairwise commutative elements). Return: ideal of two-sided generators (not a Groebner basis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute intersection of M with the subalgebra generated by Z (usually Z is the center). Note: central.lib's central() can be used to obtain Z. Example shows computing intersections in parametric U(sl2) and returning explicit generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncfactor.lib (library overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Library: ncfactor.lib. Purpose: Tools for factorization in certain noncommutative algebras (Weyl, shift, graded q-Weyl).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overview describes implemented algorithms for factorization in several algebra types, references to authors and publications, and link to more details. Procedures include ncfactor, facWeyl, facFirstWeyl, testNCfac, facSubWeyl, facShift, facFirstShift, homogfacNthQWeyl, homogfacFirstQWeyl, homogfacNthQWeyl_all, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncfactor
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ncfactor(h); h a polynomial in a non-commutative polynomial algebra over a field k. Return: list(list) of factorizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute all factorizations of h. Theory/assume: ansatz-driven method; requires k such that factorize can factor commutative univariate/multivariate polynomials and at least one variable exists in ring. Note: each output entry is a list of factors for one factorization; first factor is always a constant (1 if none excluded). Example demonstrates returned lists of factors for a polynomial in U(sl2). See related facWeyl, facSubWeyl, testNCfac.

rubrics_metrics.name: facWeyl
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: facWeyl(h); h a polynomial in the n-th Weyl algebra. Return: list of factorizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute all factorizations in the first Weyl algebra using algorithm by Heinle and Levandovskyy. Assume: basering is nth Weyl algebra. Note: output format similar to ncfactor (first entry constant). Example shows factoring (d1+1)^2*(d1 + x1*d2). See facFirstWeyl, facSubWeyl, testNCfac for related functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: facFirstWeyl
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: facFirstWeyl(h); h a polynomial in the first Weyl algebra. Return: list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: wrapper for facWeyl for compatibility with older versions (downward-compatible). Assume basering is first Weyl algebra. Note: output entries are lists representing factorizations; example provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: testNCfac
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: testNCfac(l[,p,b]); l a list of factor lists, p optional polynomial, b optional flag 0/1. Return: either 1/0 or list of differences depending on args.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: check whether entries in l represent same polynomial or factorization of p. Cases: (1) no p: returns 1 if all entries in l represent same polynomial, else 0. (2) with p: returns 1 if entries in l are factorizations of p else 0. (3) with p and b=1: returns list of differences product(entry)-p for each entry. Assume basering is first Weyl algebra and entries are polynomials. Example shows correct and incorrect cases and use of third arg to get differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: facSubWeyl
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: facSubWeyl(h,[x1,...,xn,d1,...,dn]); h polynomial in basering, xi,di variables. Return: list(list) of factorizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: xi,di generate a copy of first Weyl algebra in basering with di*xi = xi*di + 1 and h depends only on those variables. If variable list omitted, function tries to detect subalgebra itself. Purpose: compute factorizations of polynomial depending on xi,di. Note: errors if variables not aligned or h not in suitable subalgebra. Example demonstrates factoring and mapping results for comparison with facFirstWeyl and testNCfac to validate.

rubrics_metrics.name: facShift
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: facShift(h); h polynomial in n-th shift algebra. Return: list of factorizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute all factorizations in n-th shift algebra. Theory: currently maps to general factorization algorithm for G-Algebras (no specialized graded algorithm yet). Note: each output entry is a list of factors; examples demonstrate multiple factorizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: facFirstShift
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: facFirstShift(h); h polynomial in first shift algebra. Return: list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: wrapper for facShift for downward compatibility with older versions. Assume basering is first shift algebra. Note: output format same as facShift; examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: homogfacNthQWeyl
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: homogfacNthQWeyl(h); h homogeneous polynomial in n-th q-Weyl algebra w.r.t. weight vector [-1,...,-1,1,...,1] (n/2,n/2 split). Return: list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute a factorization of an [-1,1]-homogeneous polynomial in n-th q-Weyl algebra. Theory: output lists describe factors; for each i, if degree in [di,xi] is k>0 then last k entries are xi (or di) as described. Assumptions: basering is nth Weyl algebra with first n variables x1..xn and next n variables d1..dn and parameters q1..qn available. Example shows factor list and ordering of variable factors. See homogfacFirstQWeyl and homogfacNthQWeyl_all for variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: homogfacFirstQWeyl
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: homogfacFirstQWeyl(h); h homogeneous polynomial in first q-Weyl algebra w.r.t weight vector [-1,1]. Return: list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: wrapper for homogfacNthQWeyl (downward-compatible) to factor homogeneous polynomials in first q-Weyl algebra. Example demonstrates factoring a polynomial into components such as x5d5+x3d3+4 and x5d5+6.

rubrics_metrics.name: homogfacNthQWeyl_all
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: homogfacNthQWeyl_all(h); h [-1,...,-1,1,...,1]-homogeneous in n-th q-Weyl algebra. Return: list of all factorizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute all possible factorizations (lists for each factorization) of homogeneous polynomial in n-th q-Weyl algebra. Assumptions same as homogfacNthQWeyl. Example shows many returned factorizations enumerated; output format is lists of lists representing each factorization.
